A.explanation: This would reduce the nucleon number by 1, but a $^{0}_{1}\beta^{+}$ carries $0$ nucleons so $P$ must stay at $23$.

B.explanation: This changes both numbers incorrectly, as the $\beta^{+}$ has mass number $0$ and charge $+1$, not mass $1$.

C.explanation: Nucleon conservation gives $23 = P + 0$ and charge conservation gives $12 = Q + 1$, so $P = 23$ and $Q = 11$.

D.explanation: This keeps $P = 23$ but adds the $+1$ charge to $12$, whereas the emitted $\beta^{+}$ charge must be subtracted from the parent proton number.

walkthrough: Identify the notation: top number is nucleon number $A$ and bottom number is proton number $Z$. Here $^{23}_{12}\text{Mg}$ decays to $^{P}_{Q}\text{X}$ plus $^{0}_{1}\beta^{+}$.
Apply conservation of nucleon number: total top on left equals total top on right, so $23 = P + 0$.
Solve for $P$: $P = 23 - 0 = 23$, so the mass number is unchanged.
Apply conservation of charge or proton number: total bottom on left equals total bottom on right, so $12 = Q + 1$.
Solve for $Q$: $Q = 12 - 1 = 11$, showing one proton is lost when the $\beta^{+}$ is emitted.
The pair $P = 23$, $Q = 11$ matches the table row with $23$ and $11$. This is option C.
